scope: one camera and one lighting mode for the Blender-mapped, Blender-baked and Isaac renders
photometric_equivalence_why: Cycles and RTX differ in BSDF, sampling and colour management; the fixture fixes the declared inputs, it does not make the images equal. Claiming equivalence is a defect, not a result.

camera.vertical_aperture_note: Kept at USD's own default. Whether the renderer follows the horizontal or the vertical aperture is what the FOV probe measures; until it has run, the fixture declares both values rather than deriving one from the resolution aspect.
camera.aperture_source: Isaac currently writes only focalLength (render_worker.py _setup_camera), so its horizontal aperture is USD's default 20.955 mm. The unified fixture authors that value explicitly in both renderers instead of letting one side default and the other hand-code 22.044444 mm.
camera.aperture_choice_why: 20.955 keeps the Isaac framing that all existing Isaac captures were taken at; the Blender side moves onto it. Changing the Isaac side instead would invalidate more evidence.

fov_check.why: Which fit rule RTX applies to an authored aperture (horizontal as-is, or scaled by the aperture/resolution aspect) is measured, not assumed. Until the probe runs, the equality of the two horizontal fields of view is unverified.

interior_fill.why: One ceiling fill, no sun. The sun is the largest uncontrolled term between the two renderers, so a mode that carries it cannot separate a material loss from a lighting difference. Ambient alone was tried first and is unusable here: the room is sealed apart from its openings, so a dome outside it lights the interior through the windows only and both renders came out near black.
interior_fill.exposure_calibration: Each renderer is driven by its own units, calibrated to a comparable mean luminance so neither image is black or clipped -- the recorded pair was 28 percent clipped white on the Blender side against a mean of 41 on the Isaac side, which is not a comparison anyone can judge materials from. Equivalence is still not claimed; the calibrated values and the measured means go in the report.

blender.calibrated_from: 50 W measured mean 201 (28% clipped) at 512px bake, bedroom case

isaac.calibrated_from: 500 measured mean 41, then 500 with the dome at 100 measured mean 27.6

room_like.why: The room lighting already used for the recorded pair and Isaac replays, reproduced so those numbers can be replayed. It is never a verdict: with the sun and the fill both on, a material loss and a lighting difference cannot be told apart.

checklist_note: Every item starts at not_run. Only a human fills these in; an assistant visual inspection is recorded as such and does not count. glass_approximation_acceptable covers ADR-008: opacity=1-transmission keeps the camera-visible reflection mix but not refraction, so it cannot be passed as lossless.
